title: Evidence-Driven Semantic Modeling of a Classical Guitar Curriculum: OWL 2 DL Validation, SWRL Reasoning, Competency Questions, and Reproducibility Support
content: This study examines how an official curriculum can be represented and evaluated as an ontology while keeping the asserted model, inferred knowledge, and supporting validation evidence explicitly distinguishable. To address this problem, an evidence-driven ontology-engineering workflow was applied to the official six-level classical-guitar curriculum for Greek Music Schools, centered on ClassicalGuitarOntology v1.6.0. All 132 targeted learning objectives were represented across six curriculum levels. We structurally audited the ontology, ran HermiT classification, and checked the OWL 2 DL profile with ROBOT before freezing it as the authoritative baseline. We then developed a separate SWRL supplement using an OWL-first rule-admission criterion. The two accepted rules produced exactly the novel rule-head assertions expected from independently computed structural joins: 468 alignsWith assertions for R01 and 11 achievesSkill assertions for R02. Combined execution produced five additional alignsWith assertions through R02-to-R01 chaining, with no unexpected or missing outputs in the corresponding validation sets. Eight asserted-knowledge and four inference-dependent Competency Questions were evaluated using SPARQL under controlled provenance conditions. Cross-phase traceability and integrity-verified preservation of research artefacts linked requirements, validation evidence, reasoning outputs, and query results. The resulting workflow combines formal validation, selective rule-based reasoning, provenance-aware evaluation, and reproducibility support for the modeled curriculum.
